clauses.reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. The operative order revises the fourth condition of the approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Needlework Industry in Puerto Rico; the revised condition continues as part of that approval, amended, until the approval ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, strike-and-insert). The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6870A is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6870-modifying-order-approving-code-fair-competition-for-the-needlework.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (3243c055d6bd...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2025-43, captured 2025-10-08T21:39:31Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6870-A—Modifying Order Approving Code of Fair Competition for the Needlework Industry in Puerto Rico to Alter the Constitution of the Puerto Rican Needlework Commission' and whose date is 1934-10-11; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('Oct 11, 1934.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6870-A—Modifying Order Approving Code of Fair Competition for the Needlework Industry in Puerto Rico to Alter the Constitution of the Puerto Rican Needlework Commission', 1934-10-11) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 593: 'Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Needle Industry in Puerto Rico approved.'). The WPA list calls the order 'Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Needle Industry in Puerto Rico approved'; the held text instead revises the fourth condition of the June 28, 1934 approval of the Needlework Industry code for Puerto Rico (the approving order is held as EO 6756-B), so the WPA summary is a looser description of the same order, with number, date and industry agreeing. EO 6870-A (October 11, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) recites the fourth condition of the June 28, 1934 approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Needlework Industry in Puerto Rico (that the Administrator appoint, within ten days of the effective date, a three-person Puerto Rican Needlework Commission with members nominated by the Puerto Rican Code Authority, the continental related-industry Code Authorities and the National Recovery Administration), recites that the continental Code Authorities cannot agree upon a nominee and the Board recommended a modification, and orders that the quoted provision 'be and it is hereby revised to read as follows: ''That there shall be established a Puerto Rican Needlework Commission consisting of four members who shall be appointed by the National Industrial Recovery Board''' (one member for the Puerto Rican industry with one vote, two for the continental related industries with one-half vote each, and an impartial chairman with one vote). The machine inventory was a single clause starting inside the quotation of the old condition, so the inventory is corrected to two clauses: the revising order and the replacement condition with its appointment direction. Legal reading: both clauses modify a condition of a section 3(a) approval, which section 3(a) authorizes ('such conditions'). The Commission's only function, set out in the approving order, is to study the operation of the code against competing codes and recommend modifications of the code to the Administrator, and to recommend on piece rates; so the direction to appoint it has no operation independent of the code. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling the amended condition continues, amended, until the parent approval ends. No held record shows whether or when the Board appointed the four members; that is not needed for the end, because the Commission and the Board's duty to appoint it exist as a condition of the approval and have no object once the approval and enforcement provisions are repealed. If appointments were made earlier, that performance would not have ended the Commission's powers, which continued as part of the condition until the repeal on 1935-06-14.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. Members appointed to the Commission before the repeal, and any recommendations the Commission made, are completed acts; no held source shows either, and nothing obliges the Board to appoint after the repeal.
